title: Invalidation-batched stream rerun dispatch (moonshot, rejected)
impact: Moonshot: reactive fan-out re-queries every stream on any write to a projected column (table/column-level invalidation), so one write dirties all M streams and dispatches M reader round-trips — of which the vast majority re-hash unchanged and suppress their emission. This challenged the assumption that each dirtied stream must re-query via its own isolate message: a single write's dirtied set is a natural batch, and since each reader worker owns one serial SQLite connection, packing the reruns into one message per worker should cut message count 25:1 for free. Added an internal `SelectIfChangedBatchRequest` + worker loop, `ReaderPool.selectBatchIfChanged`, a batched `StreamEngine._flushQueue`/`_requeryBatch` (per-entry below pool size so the common case is byte-identical), and a `lastRowCount` cost-gate (batch cheap streams, dispatch large ones individually) — the private cost signal exp 239 named as its reopen condition. **Rejected.** Two measurement methods disagreed and the clean one won: an in-process A/B toggle reported homogeneous emit latency −25.8% / −27.9% (`ab_drift_check` REPRODUCED across an order flip), but a cross-worktree comparison (two separate binaries, 3 alternated rounds, warm regime) reversed the sign — the batched path is +22% p50 / +59% p95 on homogeneous fan-out and +66% p50 / +52% p95 on heterogeneous. A batched reply is indivisible, so the one changed stream's result waits behind its ~24 cheap unchanged batch-mates' re-hashes; message-count amortization is the wrong lever for a latency-bound workload (same trade rejected by exp 148 and exp 239). The in-process toggle manufactured a false win by sharing warm JIT/isolate/pool state across both arms — the durable lesson is to A/B dispatch/scheduling changes across worktrees, never a single-process toggle. Runtime reverted; prototype at `archive/exp-249`; `stream_rerun_latency.dart` kept as the single-write fan-out emission-latency gate. Reopen only for a throughput-bound stream workload where total drain dominates and per-emission latency is provably not the binding constraint.
